aspects.says: A constant variable's value is copied into the classes that read it, so recompiling only its declaring class doesn't change them, and reading it doesn't initialize the class.
basis: section:A Constant Variable Is Compiled Into the Code That Reads It

aspects.says: A static initializer that throws is never run again: the first use gets ExceptionInInitializerError and every later use NoClassDefFoundError until the JVM restarts.
basis: section:A Static Initializer That Throws Leaves the Class Unusable Until the JVM Restarts

aspects.says: final on a static field fixes the reference, not the object, so a mutable object in it is shared by concurrent callers; immutable or concurrent objects are safe there.
basis: section:A Static Field Is One Variable Shared by Every Object and Every Thread

aspects.says: A class is initialized on its first active use (new, a static method call, a non-constant static field it declares, Class.forName, a subclass's initialization), superclass first; a class literal, forName with false, an array type, a constant or an inherited field read through a subclass don't initialize it.
basis: section:A Class Is Initialized on Its First Active Use, Not When Its Name Appears

aspects.says: Work that can fail belongs in a method that can be called again, not in a static initializer; a holder class makes the load lazy but not retryable.
basis: section:A Static Initializer That Throws Leaves the Class Unusable Until the JVM Restarts

aspects.says: A static method can't use this or an instance field, and a static field reached through an instance is still the one static field.
aspects.reason: the first is a compile error and the second compiles to the same static access, so no wrong solution that compiles behaves differently in a test

aspects.says: A static field is one variable for the whole class, read and written by every object and every thread that uses the class.
basis: section:A Static Field Is One Variable Shared by Every Object and Every Thread

aspects.says: A class loaded through two class loaders is two classes with two sets of static fields.
aspects.reason: a lookup fact in the Reference; the rate-card practice's tests use it to start each test with an uninitialized class, but nothing the reader writes depends on it

aspects.says: Static initializers run top to bottom, so a static instance created before a later static field reads that field's default.
basis: section:Static Initializers Run in Source Order, So an Early One Reads a Later Field's Default
